hints.title: State Parity Decoupling
hints.text: Maintain separate counters for subsequences terminating with even and odd integers.

hints.title: Transition Extensions
hints.text: An incoming value can append to existing alternating subsequences or initiate a new singleton sequence.

hints.title: Modulo Aggregation
hints.text: Combine both terminal state counters modulo 10^9 + 7 after processing all elements.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def numberOfEffectiveSubsequences(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        # Effective subsequence: strictly increasing with distinct parity endpoints modulo 10^9+7
        # Or non-empty subsequence whose elements satisfy a dynamic state condition
        MOD = 1_000_000_007
        # dp[0]: count of effective subsequences ending in even value
        # dp[1]: count of effective subsequences ending in odd value
        dp0 = 0
        dp1 = 0
        for x in nums:
            if x % 2 == 0:
                # Can extend any previous odd subsequence or start new
                new_dp0 = (dp0 + dp1 + 1) % MOD
                dp0 = new_dp0
            else:
                # Can extend any previous even subsequence or start new
                new_dp1 = (dp1 + dp0 + 1) % MOD
                dp1 = new_dp1
        return (dp0 + dp1) % MOD
```

complexity.notes: Single pass state-machine dynamic programming with constant transitions.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining all 2^N subsequences produces exponential runtime.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use 2-state dynamic programming to count qualifying subsequences in linear time.
